The Renewal Meeting

Same story for both of you, only the questions are split. You ask, your partner searches the text and answers. Then switch. This review pulls together everything from the Grammar Lab: plans and spontaneous decisions, hypothetical risk, and the difference between opinion, agreement, and rule.

Alex, walking Michael and Sarah through the renewal numbers before the call with Norvex.

Odd-numbered items are your guesses, ask your partner. Even-numbered items are theirs, listen and search the text.

TEXT A · FUTURE · The Plan for Friday

The renewal meeting with Norvex is set for Friday, and Alex has been preparing all week. Northwind is going to present two options: the standard plan and an extended plan with faster response times. Alex is going to open with the actual numbers Emma pulled last month, not with a sales pitch, that decision was made days ago.

During the call yesterday, Michael mentioned a scheduling conflict, and Alex reacted immediately: "That's fine, I 'll adjust my calendar," he said. Sarah is going to join for the first ten minutes only, she already has another commitment right after. Julia won't attend in person, but she's going to send written comments on the contract language before Friday. Northwind's regional director is going to call in from another office just to observe, that was arranged weeks ago.

TEXT B · SECOND CONDITIONAL · Imagining the Risk

Alex knows the numbers alone won't convince anyone, so he built a short hypothesis into his opening. "If Norvex let the contract lapse, the plant would lose priority response on emergency callouts," that's the first point he wants to land. "If the maintenance dropped to the basic plan, Emma's vibration monitoring would stop covering two of the four compressors, and nobody at Norvex would notice until something failed."

Alex isn't predicting disaster, he's just inviting Michael and Sarah to picture it for a moment. "If a compressor failed during a night shift with no coverage, how much would that actually cost the plant in lost production?" If Norvex's legal team read the current contract without context, they might not even notice how much protection it gives them, that's actually one of Alex's stronger points. Alex would rather show the risk clearly now than have Michael discover it the hard way later.

TEXT C · SHOULD · SUPPOSED TO · MUST · The Recommendation

Near the end, Alex shifts from risk to recommendation, and here the language gets very precise. "In my opinion, Norvex should keep the extended plan, it gives you more room if something goes wrong," he says, careful to frame it as his personal view, not a rule. Then he points to the current agreement: "The plan is supposed to include two inspections a year, that's what's already written into it, whether you renew the extended option or not."

Julia's written comment, read aloud by Michael, is stricter: "Any safety-critical equipment must be inspected before the contract renewal date, this isn't negotiable, it's company policy." Alex nods and adds one more thing, gently: "You don't have to decide today, but a decision is supposed to reach us by the fifteenth, and that date is getting close." Nobody promises anything in the room, but by the time the call ends, Sarah has already asked David to draft the paperwork for the extended plan.
